faq.q: How does a BC foreclosure start?
faq.a: By petition in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under Rule 21-7 (1); everyone whose interest in the property is sought to be extinguished must be made a respondent, and the petitioner must serve the court's foreclosure information notice, Form 125, with the petition.

faq.q: What does court confirmation mean for my offer on an Abbotsford home?
faq.a: The person with conduct of sale applies under Rule 21-7 (9) for an order confirming the sale, directing the disposition of the proceeds and vesting title in the purchaser — and that application can be made even before the redemption period expires, so until the order is made the sale is not final.

faq.q: Where can I check the court file for an Abbotsford foreclosure?
faq.a: Court Services Online offers eSearch to anyone with Internet access; Supreme Court civil file details include the file number, registry, party names and filed documents, and foreclosure files are class "H - Foreclosure". Abbotsford also has its own Supreme Court registry at 32375 Veterans Way for in-person registry inquiries.

faq.q: What is a court-ordered sale in Abbotsford Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: It is a sale of a property supervised by the court after a lender has taken legal action, and the sale needs court approval. Offers are usually made subject to that approval, and other buyers can sometimes bid higher at the hearing.

faq.q: Can I put conditions on an offer for a foreclosure in Abbotsford Foreclosures and Court Sales?
faq.a: Conditions such as financing or inspection may be limited or not accepted, depending on the lender's and the court's terms. Speak to Jared and your lawyer before you write an offer.
